insider_note: A one-line definition question. Say 'without soil' explicitly — that is the whole point of the technique and the word the examiner looks for.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Hydroponics defined
steps.margin_note: Two lines. The words 'nutrient solution' and 'without soil' are both needed.
lines: Hydroponics is the technique of growing plants
in a specified nutrient solution, WITHOUT soil.
steps.why: Soil normally supplies both support and minerals, so removing it is what lets each mineral be supplied on its own and studied.
common_mistakes: Leaving out 'without soil'. That is the defining feature.
Saying plants are grown in water alone. It is a NUTRIENT solution, not plain water.
steps.memory_tip: Hydro means water: the roots sit in solution, not soil.

steps.label: What it shows
steps.margin_note: One line on the purpose. This is the half most answers skip.

lines.text: Leave one element out and see what fails

lines: Because every element in the solution is known,
hydroponics is used to find which elements are
essential and what their deficiency symptoms
steps.why: A known solution can have exactly one element removed, and whatever goes wrong afterwards must be that element's job.
common_mistakes: Giving only the definition. The second mark is for what hydroponics is used for.
Saying it is used to grow crops faster. Its use here is to study essential elements.
steps.memory_tip: Control the solution and the plant tells you what is missing.
